title: HelixCare pilot - throughput insights & playbook review
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last 48h throughput runs, discuss continuous batching behavior at 800-1k QPS equivalent, tune concurrency targets and queueing strategy, and agree on next steps for a performance comparison against their in-house batching layer. Action items include running a 4-hour steady-state run, sharing a trimmed benchmark spreadsheet, and scheduling a side-by-side latency QPS test next Tuesday.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-08 15:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (HelixCare), Tom (HelixCare), Sara (Product), Victor (Security)

Summary / Quick notes: Marcus uploaded new run results from the last 48 hours; observed a spike in p95 when concurrency jumped above target; continuous batching generally increased throughput but added tail latency at certain queue depths; KV cache hit helped for repeated prompts.

00:00 Lena: okay everyone thanks for hopping on, we'll do a quick run through of the numbers Marcus shared and then talk tuning playbook, if anyone has constraints please flag them.
00:18 Marcus: yeah i put the spreadsheet in the shared drive, link in the calendar note, it's the trimmed version with per-model and per-shard p50 p95 p99 and token counts, umm note that the model in the pilot is the 13B quantized variant so numbers are a touch different than float.
00:36 Priya: got it, i skimmed it earlier, saw the p95 bump around the 21:00 UTC mark, is that when you changed the concurrency?
00:45 Marcus: sort of, we bumped the concurrency target for the worker pool from 28 to 42 to chase throughput, that pushed more into larger batches, which normally helps ops but we saw an odd tail. might be queueing/backpressure interplay.
01:02 Tom: can you remind me of the request profile - avg tokens per request and how many streaming clients? we run a bunch of short instruction-following prompts and some long summarizations.
01:12 Marcus: the trimmed profile shows median tokens ~120, 90th at 512, heavy tail from summarizers; QPS equivalent was about 550 sustained with bursts to ~1k for 10s. streaming clients 40% of traffic; also prefix caching reduced token compute for repeat templates.
01:31 Sara: so is the issue that continuous batching is making big batches and that's causing the p95 to go up? or is it concurrency oversubscribing the GPU?
01:40 Marcus: it's both, there's this interaction: continuous batching gathers requests which is great, but if queue depth creeps past our threshold the batch sizes increase and individual latency sees climb; while GPU occupancy improves overall, the p95 can degrade because some requests wait for a larger batch.
01:59 Lena: that's the classic throughput/latency tradeoff. are we using the adaptive batch timeout?
02:06 Marcus: yes, adaptive timeout is on; we also have request prioritization where short prompts get higher priority but it doesn't always win when the backlog forms. i think tuning the concurrency cap is the lever here and maybe tightening the max batch size or lowering the batch_wait_ms for low-latency routes.
02:26 Victor: from security side, any changes to logging or KMS usage during the run? we noted a couple audit gaps last week.
02:33 Marcus: no changes to KMS; logs were intact, i will attach audit snippet but there's some scrubbing we need to do.
02:40 Priya: quick question - you mentioned KV cache hit rate was 37% overall, can that be improved by pre-warming?
02:48 Marcus: yes pre-warming with our prefix cache helps; we saw hit rate go up to 62% for a subset when we pre-seeded repeated templates, that cut compute by about 28% for that slice.
03:02 Tom: i want to understand concurrency targets - you suggested 40-60 earlier, what's the recommended for our workload?
03:09 Marcus: based on token distribution and GPU type (A10x2 in test harness) starting point is 36 for steady-state, bump to 48 for burst tolerance; but the playbook recommends running a 4-hour steady-state at each concurrency setting (36/48/60) and check p50/p95/cost per token.
03:30 Lena: can we run the costing calc for those three points? Chris (not present) wanted cost per 1M tokens at each setting for comparison to their in-house batching.
03:40 Marcus: yep, i'll include cost columns in the spreadsheet.
03:46 Priya: during the last run we saw p50 stable ~90ms while p95 jumped to 420ms at the worst; that worries product - UX wants p95 < 300 for live chat.
03:59 Marcus: understood; we can tighten latency by lowering max_batch_size for the chat route and enabling smaller priority buckets; that sacrifices some throughput but should pull p95 inside target.
04:12 Tom: can Redwood route between a lower-latency variant and a higher-throughput variant? like fallback to a quantized 7B for severe load?
04:21 Marcus: yes, smart routing supports model variants and fallbacks; policy can be region or latency based; we can set automated fallback to a smaller model when queue depth or latency SLOs are breached.
04:35 Priya: what's the expected quality delta for our prompts when falling back from 13B quant to the 7B? we need to include eval guidance.
04:44 Marcus: we'll run side-by-side eval on the production prompt set and include rouge/bleu-like task metrics plus human review for hallucination sensitivity; that's part of the benchmark mid next week.
04:58 Lena: okay for the playbook items i want an explicit recommendation: concurrency cap, max_batch_size, batch_wait_ms, priority rules, and fallback threshold. Marcus?
05:07 Marcus: yes i'll draft the playbook and share as a short doc. key defaults to propose: concurrency >=36 and <=48 for steady, max_batch_size 32 for chat route, batch_wait_ms 8ms for short route, fallback to 7B at queue depth >120 or p95 > 350ms sustained over 30s.
05:29 Victor: does fallback preserve token encryption and audit trails?
05:33 Marcus: yes, same KMS and audit pipeline, just a different model artifact.
05:38 Priya: are there any config changes that require redeploys or will everything be runtime flags?
05:44 Marcus: all of these are runtime route configs except if you want to change the model artifact pin permanently, that would be a deploy step. route configs can be toggled with zero downtime.
05:55 Sara: can you also include guidance for autoscaling thresholds? like when to add more dedicated capacity vs scale out pods?
06:03 Marcus: recommended autoscale: add burst capacity when sustained QPS > 85% of lane for 5m, add instance at 60% CPU+90% GPU util sustained for 2m; but for Dedicated we prefer scaling whole GPU pool. I'll put exact thresholds in playbook.
06:26 Tom: for the 4-hour runs we'll need a test harness - can Redwood kick off the run or should we run from our side?
06:34 Lena: we can coordinate; Marcus can provide the load script and expected tokens, HelixCare will run it under their network to mimic real egress and latency characteristics.
06:44 Marcus: i'll attach a k6 script and a docker runner, plus instructions for preserving request ids to correlate traces.
06:53 Priya: great. also, please include a short section on cost optimization - quantization profiles and recommended batching windows per workload.
07:01 Marcus: noted. We'll include quantization notes: 8-bit dynamic and offload steps that helped for the 13B.
07:12 Lena: any blockers from legal/procurement? Victor?
07:15 Victor: a couple of audit items but nothing blocking the pilot; i'll email the notes.
07:22 Lena: cool, let's recap next steps.
07:26 Marcus: recap - share spreadsheet and playbook draft, HelixCare to run steady-state runs, schedule side-by-side QPS test on Tuesday.
07:34 Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.

41:35 Lena: end of call, closing notes and link to resources: drive/helixcare/pilot-results, doc/playbook-draft, k6-runner repo.
41:50 call ended.
questions: What concurrency cap produces acceptable p95 for chat?
Can fallback to 7B maintain acceptable quality for our summarization prompts?
How to balance batch_wait_ms and max_batch_size for mixed short/long workloads?
